answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive overview of **Medi-Cal** — California's Medicaid program — and the key changes happening in 2026 and beyond:

---

## 🏥 What is Medi-Cal?
**Medi-Cal** is California's free or low-cost health insurance program for low-income individuals and families, funded jointly by the state and federal government.

---

## 📋 Key Medi-Cal Changes (2026–2028)

### ✅ January 1, 2026 – Enrollment Freeze for Undocumented Adults
Beginning January 1, 2026, new Medi-Cal applications for adults (ages 19 and up) who are undocumented can only qualify for Emergency Medi-Cal or pregnancy-related Medi-Cal.

However, if you already have Medi-Cal or if you applied before January 1, 2026, you are eligible to keep your full-scope Medi-Cal coverage, provided you still meet all other eligibility requirements.

---

### 💰 January 1, 2026 – Asset Limit Reinstated
Effective January 1, 2026, the asset limit will be reinstated for non-MAGI Medi-Cal programs, back to 2022 levels — $130,000 for an individual, and $65,000 for each additional household member.

Medi-Cal will review 30 months of your financial history. Transfers, gifts, and trust funding done at the wrong time or the wrong way can trigger months or even years of ineligibility.

---

### 🦷 July 1, 2026 – Dental Coverage Changes
Starting July 1, 2026, some Medi-Cal members will stop getting full-scope dental services as part of their Medi-Cal coverage.

Dental benefits will not be covered for Medi-Cal members ages 19 and up who are undocumented or who do not have satisfactory immigration status.

---

### 🌍 October 1, 2026 – Immigration Status Reclassification
Starting October 1, 2026, the federal government will change how it classifies some immigration statuses. This may affect eligibility for full-scope Medi-Cal for certain groups such as refugees and asylees.

---

### 📅 January 1, 2027 – More Frequent Renewals
Effective January 1, 2027, adults ages 19–64 will need to renew Medi-Cal every **six months** instead of annually. Missing deadlines could result in loss of coverage.

### 💼 January 1, 2027 – Work Requirements
Starting January 1, 2027, some adults will need to work, volunteer, or go to school to keep Medi-Cal. If this applies to you, the county Medi-Cal office will send you a letter.

---

### 💵 October 1, 2028 – Copayments Begin
Beginning October 1, 2028, some adults on Medi-Cal will pay small copayments for certain services, capped at 5% of household income, with **no copays** for emergency care, checkups, pregnancy, pediatric, mental health, or community clinic services.

---

## 📌 What Most Members Should Know

Most Medi-Cal members will keep the same eligibility and benefits. Covered benefits include seeing your doctor, going to the hospital, emergency care, filling prescriptions, mental health supports, substance use treatment, regular checkups, vaccines, long-term care, non-emergency medical transportation, dental, and vision care.

---

## ✅ Action Steps to Stay Covered

1. Make sure to keep your Medi-Cal information updated so you don't miss important notices. Know your renewal date so you can renew your Medi-Cal online or work with your local county Medi-Cal office.
2. Make sure your address and contact information are current, and review and respond to all mail from the county. If you get a yellow renewal packet, fill it out and return it by the due date.
3. Keep going to the doctor and other medical appointments, and ask about available telehealth services.

---
